speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is truly the most important gift that we give to our young.” The Prime Minister went on to outline a vision for a refreshed education sector, one that recognises and rewards individual differences and preferences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As some of you may recall, GK Chesterton was an English author and philosopher.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: To explain, I will quote Mr Chesterton himself: "Chesterton's Fence is the principle that reforms should not be made until the reasoning behind the existing state of affairs is understood.” Mr Speaker, let us imagine that there is a fence or gate erected across a road.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As Chesterton writes: “The more modern type of reformer goes gaily up to it and says, ‘I don’t see the use of this; let us clear it away.’ To which the more intelligent type of reformer will do well to answer: ‘If you don’t see the use of it, I certainly won’t let you clear it away.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Then, when you can come back and tell me that you do see the use of it, I may allow you to destroy it.’” This principle reminds us to understand the purpose and value of existing ways of doing things before making changes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is unwise to rush towards change for change sake, as there are frequently very good reasons for doing things a certain way, even if those reasons have long been forgotten.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In making change, it is important to preserve what is beneficial and innovate only where necessary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: So, to all the teachers, counsellors and ancillary staff out there who may be listening, thank you for everything you do.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Your commitment to the teaching, education and well-being of our children is noticed and welcomed across Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And in doing different, we must ensure that those working in schools and across the sector are provided with the training, supervision, support and time needed to do their job.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In doing so, I will first discuss some of the qualitative characteristics of an effective education system, followed by a summary of several quantitative indicators that could potentially be used to measure successful implementation of those characteristics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We can always do things better and differently and Singapore has never shied away from such a challenge.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I should also note that many of the issues I am about to highlight have previously been identified by Members of this Parliament and other commentators, including Prime Minister Wong in his National Day Rally speech.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: So, I am, as they say, standing on the shoulder of giants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Schools will give equal attention to the physical, emotional, social and intellectual health, and well-being of children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Children will no longer be assessed or judged by a mark or a grade, but by their personal progress towards individualised goals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We will actively encourage and support children to pursue studies and careers of personal passion, interest and emotional reward; and not those imposed externally by families, friends or society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Critical thinking, problem-solving, collaboration and adaptability will be seen as core skills for children, alongside reading, writing, spelling and other more traditional subjects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Arts and humanities will be of equal personal and academic value as other technical subjects and schools will be sufficiently resourced to enable children to successfully pursue and graduate in those subjects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Education and learning will be seen as a shared and equal responsibility between schools, parents and children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Children will feel safe, welcome and happy at school; and schools will have safeguarding policies and procedures that are co-designed between schools, parents and children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Now that I have described what a school of the future might look like, how will we know when we get there?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We will recognise that examinations suit some children, but not all children; and that a low mark or, indeed, any mark in an examination is not always a valid or reliable indicator of a child's immediate or long-term capacity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We will, instead, employ a suite of continuous assessment methodologies that recognise that children learn and demonstrate proficiency and delight in their learning, in many different ways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We will no longer stream children primarily on academic performance, but will, instead, recognise the unique and individual strengths of each child and will focus on assisting children to transition seamlessly into a school and class of choice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We will not talk about gifted children but instead, consider that all children are gifted in different ways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Homework will be an exception rather than the rule, with the bulk of the school curriculum being successfully taught within school hours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Out-of-school tutoring will no longer be the norm, with children having individualised, in-school learning plans that provide them with what they need and want academically, socially and emotionally.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Children will return home from school to play with their siblings, friends and family; not to focus predominantly on study or training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Weekends will be an opportunity for families to spend time together playing at home or in the park, going for walks, watching movies, visiting galleries or just talking with each other; not rushing from appointment to appointment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: School holidays will be exactly as the term suggests: a holiday.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Children will put away their schoolbooks and do what children are supposed to be doing: learning through play.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Children will attend their school of choice, and all schools will provide children access to the same level and quality of services and facilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Teachers will have work hours, a workload and work environment that actively promotes and protects job satisfaction, positive mental health and personal well-being.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Social status and privilege will play no part in a child's access to school nor the child's success at school.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We will recognise that the level of stress, distress and anxiety currently experienced by many children, often because of performance or assessment obligations and expectations, is unhealthy, unnecessary and counterproductive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And Mr Speaker, we will, as a nation and a community, do everything we can to ensure that all children are valued for who they are as people and not because of their background, family, ability, school, grade or career.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I have identified the destination, so I will now explore the journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: These stakeholders include the Government, the community, the business sector, the media, schools, teachers, parents and, of course, children themselves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Each stakeholder has their own fence: their own perspectives, preferences and agendas; and system-wide reform is more effective with the participation and endorsement of all.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to ask everyone about their fences before we remove them or build new ones.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: For example, parents push their children hard and focus on academic outcomes because the commonly held notion among Singaporeans that grades, rankings and certificates are all important.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans take this stance because that is the way it has always been done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It has served us well in the past.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Schools, therefore, maintain a system where education and assessment is competitive, comparative and task orientated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The whole cycle feeds on itself and none of the stakeholders want to be the first to change.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: All of the stakeholders mentioned above need to be on the same page.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to build a common understanding and a common purpose, and this can only be achieved by meaningful and ongoing consultation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: If we expect, for example, parents and schools to focus more on a child's happiness and well-being than their grades, we need to create a broader ecosystem where grades and outcomes are not such an all-important factor.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to create and build new common fence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We are well-placed to take a leadership role in facilitating meaningful engagement and dialogue with all relevant stakeholders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: However, we also need to be informed by contemporary best-practice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Such a group would need to comprise representatives from the Government, the business and community sectors, academics, schools, parents, health professionals, social workers and psychologists and, of course, students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans are smart people and if we want them to think or do things differently, we need to clearly explain why.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to make available to all stakeholders the evidence that a reformed education sector will not cause the sky to fall.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, it will lead to better outcomes for everyone, including, most importantly, our children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: If we expect stakeholders to shift their perspectives, to lower their fences, we need to provide evidence that there is a different, more contemporary and effective way of doing things.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Along with meaningful stakeholder engagement, we are also well-placed to develop and implement community-wide education campaigns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Southeast Asians and Singaporeans see the world in a unique way.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Many of us have deeply held and long-standing sociocultural attitudes, values and beliefs, including attitudes, values and beliefs about childhood, education, parenting and work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our way of life has served us well and Singapore is an internationally renowned success because of how we see and do things.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In reimaging education, it is essential that we do not dismantle necessary or precious fences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We do not want Singapore to be like the West nor to disregard our heritage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As we move forward, we need to bring each of Singapore's cultural communities with us and actively engage with them to safely and respectfully examine current perspectives and practices and explore new ones.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Children of parents who are actively involved in their child's learning and school community have better educational outcomes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: By working closely with the school and broader community and seeking support when needed, parents can assist and equip their children with the skills needed to contribute positively to society and to be part of a forward-thinking environment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In undertaking this role, it is important that parents encourage and support their children to explore multiple opportunities and interests and to balance traditional academic success with personal satisfaction and emotional well-being.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: An across-Government roadmap for change is one way to achieve this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Restorative justice has been of professional and academic interest to me for many years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The four principles that underpin restorative justice – respect, responsibility, reintegration and restoration – are highly relevant to the education sector and to effective teaching and learning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: For example, schools need to be places, where children are respected and where they valued and supported in all aspects of their education and learning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Schools have to be places where teachers have the time, space, resources, qualifications and desire to build and maintain respectful, effective and individualised relationships with every child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: All children in all schools need to be and to feel known by their school and teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And that, Mr Speaker, is what education is all about.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As we evolve our education system for a better tomorrow, we must remember that good outcomes depend critically on good educators who can implement our ideas consistently and with conviction.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, our success is not defined by academic results attained in the first 15 years in school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: More importantly, it is defined by our contributions in the next 50 years beyond our schools, where we continue to possess the joy of learning and the DNA to strive for excellence in diverse domains.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This starts with building a love of learning in the early years as our children explore the world and develop their bilingual, mathematics and critical thinking foundations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In their schooling years, we will provide students with porous and diverse pathways and give them opportunities to grow their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This means that no single test should determine a student's future and not every topic taught needs to be tested.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With changes like these, we hope to shift towards a mindset of learning and growth instead of an exam-oriented mindset.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond the schooling years, we will invest in our people throughout life, with SkillsFuture as a key pillar of our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We recently enhanced investments in our SkillsFuture programmes – from the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme to the JobSeeker Support scheme and training allowances for mid-career upgraders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All these allow our people to seize opportunities to stay relevant and secure good jobs that offer dignity, respect and financial sufficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, we recognise that our people have strengths in diverse areas.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These talents can manifest across time rather than at any single pre-determined point in life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, we must resist the temptation to "teach to the average" of a child or a class.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must cater to different learning needs of our children, across different life stages and provide porous systems for our children to develop at their own pace.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have improved our system over the years to allow students to customise their education at a finer level.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have enhanced our curriculum support for Special Education schools to improve their ability to cater to students with a range of special education needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are Special Needs Officers at all primary schools to better support students with mild to moderate needs who can access mainstream education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The recently announced changes to the Gifted Education Programme and Higher Mother Tongue Language eligibility criteria in Secondary 1 will provide more opportunities to stretch our students in specific areas of strength.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These moves also offer more opportunities for students to interact with peers of different profiles.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our school landscape and admissions system recognise students' diverse strengths and abilities rather than purely academic performance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For those with particular talents and aptitudes, we have Specialised Independent Schools – School of the Arts, NUS High School, Singapore Sports School and Singapore School of Science and Technology.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Aptitude-based admissions and Direct School Admission provide opportunities for students to pursue studies based on potential and interest and broaden their access to diverse education pathways.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We share similar aspirations as the Member to provide each child with a customised learning journey based on his or her individual strengths and abilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why we keep innovating and leveraging technology, including artificial intelligence, data science and the science of learning, to break the conventional education system trilemma of achieving quality at scale, speed and affordability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Through these efforts, we are striving towards mass customisation to free ourselves from the mindset that quality education is determined by class size alone.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In fact, studies have shown that the quality of teachers is most important in determining the outcomes of education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Third, trust and professional respect for educators must be the foundation of our system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will determine our society's ability to attract the best and most committed teachers, which then determines our education outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Without good teachers, even the best education policies will have limited impact.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our teachers undergo years of rigorous training to do their work as professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But respect for teachers must come not just from MOE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I seek everyone's support to respect and trust our teachers to do their jobs and to work with our teachers to support our children's learning and upbringing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Fourth, we agree with the Member that strong partnerships are essential for our students to learn for life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why we established the MOE Partnerships Engagement Office last year, to rally partners – industry, parents, community, experts – to collaborate with schools to create authentic learning opportunities for students and for us to leverage on the whole-of-society capabilities to provide the best for our children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But our most important partners are our parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We all want the best for our children, but the best may not mean the most popular school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead, we should ask which school will bring out the best version of our children so that they will learn to surpass themselves in life instead of trying to surpass others in an exam and to have confidence in their abilities instead of comparing with others to determine their self-worth.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All of us – parents, educators and public – must evolve our mindsets to complement the structural and policy changes that we are making.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We cannot and should not try to remove all uncertainties and difficulties that our children face.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Each and every setback is also a learning opportunity for our children to build resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead, we must retain space for our children to try, fail, take responsibility and bounce back from setbacks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Only then can they learn to embrace untidiness and thrive amidst uncertainties – the only things that we can be certain that the future will hold.
